     1→"""LangGraph workflow definition for the consolidated protocol processor.
     2→
     3→Defines a 7-node StateGraph for the unified protocol processing pipeline:
     4→START -> ingest -> extract -> parse -> ground -> persist
     5→     -> structure -> ordinal_resolve -> END
     6→
     7→Error routing:
     8→- After ingest, extract, parse: conditional edges route to END on error
     9→- After ground: always proceeds to persist (ground uses error accumulation)
    10→- Persist handles partial/total failures internally
    11→- Structure uses error accumulation (same as ground)
    12→- Ordinal resolve uses error accumulation (same pattern)
    13→
    14→Per user decision (v2.0 Architecture): "Flat pipeline with expression tree phase"
    15→"""
    16→
    17→import os
    18→from typing import Any
    19→
    20→from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
    21→
    22→from protocol_processor.nodes.extract import extract_node
    23→from protocol_processor.nodes.ground import ground_node
    24→from protocol_processor.nodes.ingest import ingest_node
    25→from protocol_processor.nodes.ordinal_resolve import ordinal_resolve_node
    26→from protocol_processor.nodes.parse import parse_node
    27→from protocol_processor.nodes.persist import persist_node
    28→from protocol_processor.nodes.structure import structure_node
    29→from protocol_processor.state import PipelineState
    30→
    31→
    32→def should_continue(state: PipelineState) -> str:
    33→    """Route to error END or continue to next node.
    34→
    35→    Args:
    36→        state: Current pipeline state.
    37→
    38→    Returns:
    39→        'error' if state has a fatal error, 'continue' otherwise.
    40→    """
    41→    return "error" if state.get("error") else "continue"
    42→
    43→
    44→def create_graph(checkpointer: Any = None) -> Any:
    45→    """Create and compile the 7-node protocol processing workflow graph.
    46→
    47→    The graph follows this flow:
    48→    START -> ingest -> extract -> parse -> ground -> persist
    49→         -> structure -> ordinal_resolve -> END
    50→
    51→    Conditional error routing after ingest, extract, and parse.
    52→    Ground always proceeds to persist (ground uses error accumulation).
    53→    Structure and ordinal_resolve use error accumulation (same pattern as ground).
    54→
    55→    Args:
    56→        checkpointer: Optional LangGraph checkpointer for fault-tolerant execution.
    57→            When provided, state is persisted after each node, enabling retry-from-
    58→            checkpoint. Use PostgresSaver for production. Defaults to None (no
    59→            checkpointing).
    60→
    61→    Returns:
    62→        Compiled StateGraph ready for async execution.
    63→    """
    64→    workflow = StateGraph(PipelineState)
    65→
    66→    # Add all 7 nodes
    67→    workflow.add_node("ingest", ingest_node)
    68→    workflow.add_node("extract", extract_node)
    69→    workflow.add_node("parse", parse_node)
    70→    workflow.add_node("ground", ground_node)
    71→    workflow.add_node("persist", persist_node)
    72→    workflow.add_node("structure", structure_node)
    73→    workflow.add_node("ordinal_resolve", ordinal_resolve_node)
    74→
    75→    # Entry point
    76→    workflow.add_edge(START, "ingest")
    77→
    78→    # Conditional error routing after ingest, extract, parse
    79→    for source, target in [
    80→        ("ingest", "extract"),
    81→        ("extract", "parse"),
    82→        ("parse", "ground"),
    83→    ]:
    84→        workflow.add_conditional_edges(
    85→            source,
    86→            should_continue,
    87→            {"continue": target, "error": END},
    88→        )
    89→
    90→    # Ground always proceeds to persist (error accumulation handles partials)
    91→    workflow.add_edge("ground", "persist")
    92→    # Persist proceeds to structure (expression tree building)
    93→    workflow.add_edge("persist", "structure")
    94→    workflow.add_edge("structure", "ordinal_resolve")
    95→    workflow.add_edge("ordinal_resolve", END)
    96→
    97→    return workflow.compile(checkpointer=checkpointer)
    98→
    99→
   100→# Singleton instances for reuse across outbox handler invocations.
   101→# Per Pitfall 1 from research: checkpointer is singleton, created once,
   102→# reused across all invocations. Do NOT create per-invocation.
   103→_graph = None
   104→_checkpointer = None
   105→# Context manager for PostgresSaver; kept entered for app lifetime.
   106→_checkpointer_cm: Any = None
   107→
   108→
   109→async def _get_checkpointer_async() -> Any:
   110→    """Get or create the AsyncPostgresSaver checkpointer singleton.
   111→
   112→    Creates an AsyncPostgresSaver using DATABASE_URL from the environment.
   113→    Uses the async context manager and calls asetup() to ensure checkpoint
   114→    tables exist. The context is kept open for the process lifetime.
   115→
   116→    Returns:
   117→        AsyncPostgresSaver instance configured with the application database.
   118→
   119→    Raises:
   120→        KeyError: If DATABASE_URL environment variable is not set.
   121→    """
   122→    global _checkpointer, _checkpointer_cm  # noqa: PLW0603
   123→    if _checkpointer is None:
   124→        from langgraph.checkpoint.postgres.aio import AsyncPostgresSaver
   125→
   126→        db_url = os.environ["DATABASE_URL"]
   127→        _checkpointer_cm = AsyncPostgresSaver.from_conn_string(db_url)
   128→        _checkpointer = await _checkpointer_cm.__aenter__()
   129→        await _checkpointer.asetup()  # Create checkpoint tables if they don't exist
   130→    return _checkpointer
   131→
   132→
   133→async def get_graph() -> Any:
   134→    """Get or create the compiled graph singleton.
   135→
   136→    Compiles the graph with an AsyncPostgresSaver checkpointer if DATABASE_URL
   137→    is available. Falls back to no checkpointer if DATABASE_URL is not set
   138→    (e.g. in unit tests).
   139→
   140→    Returns:
   141→        Compiled StateGraph instance.
   142→    """
   143→    global _graph  # noqa: PLW0603
   144→    if _graph is None:
   145→        try:
   146→            checkpointer = await _get_checkpointer_async()
   147→        except Exception:
   148→            # KeyError: DATABASE_URL not set; psycopg.OperationalError: DB
   149→            # unreachable (e.g. unit tests). Compile without checkpointer.
   150→            checkpointer = None
   151→        _graph = create_graph(checkpointer=checkpointer)
   152→    return _graph
   153→

     1→"""Unified outbox event handler for ProtocolUploaded events.

    11→conflicts because the outbox processor runs handlers in a thread executor

    34→def _cleanup_orphan_traces() -> None:
    35→    """Close stale IN_PROGRESS MLflow traces from previous crashed runs.
    36→
    37→    Runs once at module import (service startup). Idempotent -- safe to
    38→    call multiple times. Only closes traces older than 1 hour to avoid
    39→    closing currently-running pipelines.
    40→    """
    41→    import time as _time
    42→
    43→    tracking_uri = os.getenv("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
    44→    if not tracking_uri:
    45→        return
    46→    try:
    47→        import mlflow
    48→
    49→        client = mlflow.MlflowClient()
    50→        cutoff_ms = int((_time.time() - 3600) * 1000)  # 1 hour ago
    51→
    52→        # MLflow 3.x: search for traces with IN_PROGRESS status
    53→        try:
    54→            traces = client.search_traces(
    55→                experiment_ids=["0"],  # Default experiment
    56→                filter_string="status = 'IN_PROGRESS'",
    57→                max_results=50,
    58→            )
    59→        except (AttributeError, TypeError):
    60→            # search_traces may not exist or have different signature
    61→            logger.debug("MLflow search_traces API not available for orphan cleanup")
    62→            return
    63→
    64→        closed = 0
    65→        for trace in traces:
    66→            trace_ts = getattr(trace.info, "timestamp_ms", None) or 0
    67→            if trace_ts < cutoff_ms:
    68→                try:
    69→                    client.end_trace(

    82→        logger.debug("Orphan trace cleanup skipped (non-fatal)", exc_info=True)

   237→        protocol_id,
   238→    )
   239→
   240→    try:
   241→        # Generate unique thread_id per pipeline run to prevent checkpoint collision
   242→        # on re-extraction (same protocol_id would resume old completed checkpoint)
   243→        thread_id = f"{protocol_id}:{uuid4()}"
   244→
   245→        initial_state: dict[str, Any] = {
   246→            "protocol_id": payload["protocol_id"],
   247→            "file_uri": payload["file_uri"],
   248→            "title": payload["title"],
   249→            "batch_id": None,
   250→            "pdf_bytes": None,
   251→            "extraction_json": None,
   252→            "entities_json": None,
   253→            "grounded_entities_json": None,
   254→            "archived_reviewed_criteria": payload.get("archived_reviewed_criteria"),
   255→            "status": "processing",
   256→            "error": None,
   257→            "errors": [],
   258→        }
   259→
   260→        # Store thread_id in protocol metadata for retry_from_checkpoint lookup
   261→        try:
   262→            with Session(engine) as session:
   263→                protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
   264→                if protocol:
   265→                    meta = protocol.metadata_ or {}
   266→                    protocol.metadata_ = {
   267→                        **meta,
   268→                        "pipeline_thread_id": thread_id,
   269→                    }
   270→                    session.add(protocol)
   271→                    session.commit()
   272→        except Exception:
   273→            logger.warning(
   274→                "Failed to store pipeline_thread_id for protocol %s",
   275→                protocol_id,
   276→            )
   277→
   278→        config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}
   279→
   280→        asyncio.run(_run_pipeline(initial_state, config, payload))
   281→
   282→        logger.info(
   283→            "Protocol pipeline completed for protocol %s",
   284→            protocol_id,
   285→        )
   286→
   287→    except Exception as e:
   288→        logger.exception(
   289→            "Protocol pipeline failed for protocol %s",
   290→            protocol_id,
   291→        )
   292→        reason = _categorize_pipeline_error(e)
   293→        _update_protocol_failed(
   294→            protocol_id,
   295→            reason,
   296→            "pipeline_failed",
   297→            type(e).__name__,
   298→        )
   299→        raise
   300→
   301→
   302→async def retry_from_checkpoint(protocol_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
   303→    """Resume pipeline from last checkpoint for a failed protocol.
   304→
   305→    Passes None as the input state to graph.ainvoke, which tells LangGraph
   306→    to resume from the last saved checkpoint for the given thread_id instead
   307→    of starting from scratch. Reads thread_id from protocol.metadata_ where
   308→    it was stored during the original pipeline invocation.
   309→
   310→    Args:
   311→        protocol_id: Protocol ID — used to look up thread_id from metadata.
   312→
   313→    Returns:
   314→        Final pipeline state dict after resuming from checkpoint.
   315→    """
   316→    with Session(engine) as session:
   317→        protocol = session.get(Protocol, protocol_id)
   318→        if not protocol:
   319→            raise ValueError(f"Protocol {protocol_id} not found")
   320→        thread_id = (protocol.metadata_ or {}).get("pipeline_thread_id", protocol_id)
   321→
   322→    from protocol_processor.graph import get_graph
   323→
   324→    graph = await get_graph()
   325→    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}}
   326→    # Pass None as input — LangGraph resumes from last checkpoint
   327→    result = await graph.ainvoke(None, config)
   328→    return result
   329→

     1→"""Pipeline state definition for the 7-node protocol processor.
     2→
     3→Minimal flat state using JSON strings for complex data to minimize token usage
     4→during LangGraph state serialization between nodes.
     5→
     6→Pipeline: ingest -> extract -> parse -> ground -> persist -> structure
     7→  -> ordinal_resolve
     8→"""
     9→
    10→from typing import Literal
    11→
    12→from typing_extensions import TypedDict
    13→
    14→
    15→class PipelineState(TypedDict):
    16→    """Minimal state for the protocol processing pipeline.
    17→
    18→    Fields are populated on-demand as the pipeline progresses through nodes:
    19→    ingest -> extract -> parse -> ground -> persist
    20→
    21→    Attributes:
    22→        protocol_id: UUID of the protocol being processed. Always present.
    23→        file_uri: GCS URI (gs://) or local path (local://) of the PDF.
    24→        title: Protocol title from upload metadata. Always present.
    25→        batch_id: UUID of the CriteriaBatch created by parse. None until then.
    26→        pdf_bytes: Raw PDF bytes. Populated by ingest, consumed by extract.
    27→        extraction_json: JSON string of extracted criteria from extract node.
    28→        entities_json: JSON string of entities for grounding from parse node.
    29→        grounded_entities_json: JSON string of grounded results from ground.
    30→        status: Current pipeline status. Updated by each node.
    31→        error: Fatal error message. Set on unrecoverable failure; routes to END.
    32→        errors: Accumulated non-fatal errors (e.g. individual grounding failures).
    33→            Partial failures are preserved alongside successes per user decision.
    34→    """
    35→
    36→    # Input (always present)
    37→    protocol_id: str
    38→    file_uri: str
    39→    title: str
    40→
    41→    # Created by parse node
    42→    batch_id: str | None
    43→
    44→    # Processing artifacts (populated on-demand)
    45→    pdf_bytes: bytes | None  # Populated by ingest, used by extract
    46→    extraction_json: str | None  # Populated by extract, used by parse
    47→    entities_json: str | None  # Populated by parse/ground
    48→    grounded_entities_json: str | None  # Populated by ground, used by persist
    49→
    50→    # Re-extraction context (optional, only present during re-extraction)
    51→    archived_reviewed_criteria: list[dict] | None
    52→
    53→    # Ordinal resolution (populated by ordinal_resolve node)
    54→    ordinal_proposals_json: str | None  # JSON of proposed ordinal scale configs
    55→
    56→    # Output
    57→    status: Literal["processing", "completed", "failed"]
    58→    error: str | None
    59→    errors: list[str]  # Accumulate partial failures per user decision

## File Summary Report

### **Protocol Processor Pipeline Nodes**

#### 1. **ingest.py**
- **Purpose**: First node in the LangGraph pipeline. Fetches PDF bytes from GCS or local storage and updates protocol status to 'extracting'.
- **Key Functions**: `ingest_node()` - async handler that fetches PDF via `fetch_pdf_bytes()` tool and updates DB status.
- **Notable Patterns**: 
  - Error propagation (returns empty dict if state has error)
  - Database session management (imports from api-service for cross-service DB access)
  - Distributed tracing with `pipeline_span` context manager
  - Returns state dict with `pdf_bytes` and `status="processing"`

#### 2. **extract.py**
- **Purpose**: Second node. Calls Gemini API with structured output for criteria extraction from PDF.
- **Key Functions**: `extract_node()` - delegates to `extract_criteria_structured()` tool using Gemini File API.
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - Thin orchestration layer (actual LLM logic in tools)
  - Returns JSON string (not dict) to minimize LangGraph state size
  - LLM span type for tracing

#### 3. **parse.py**
- **Purpose**: Third node. Parses extraction JSON into DB records (CriteriaBatch, Criteria) and decomposes criteria into medical entities.
- **Key Functions**: 
  - `parse_node()` - main handler
  - Creates CriteriaBatch and Criteria records
  - Calls `decompose_entities_from_criterion()` concurrently via `asyncio.gather()`
  - Builds entity_items with fallback category→type mapping
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - Phase A (DB persistence) + Phase B (async entity decomposition) split
  - State size optimization: clears pdf_bytes after extraction
  - Accumulates field_mappings for multiple entities per criterion
  - Runs entity decomposition OUTSIDE DB session (avoids holding sessions during LLM calls)

#### 4. **ground.py**
- **Purpose**: Fourth node. Routes entities via TerminologyRouter, selects best match with MedGemma, generates field mappings.
- **Key Functions**:
  - `ground_node()` - main orchestrator
  - `_ground_entity_with_retry()` - implements agentic retry loop (max 3 attempts)
  - `_ground_entity_parallel()` - concurrency control with semaphore
  - `_reconcile_dual_grounding()` - merges TerminologyRouter + OMOP mapper results
  - `_log_grounding_audit()` - audit trail to AuditLog table
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - Error accumulation (individual entity failures don't block pipeline)
  - Dual grounding: TerminologyRouter + OMOP mapper run in parallel per entity
  - Agentic reasoning loop: if confidence < 0.5, asks MedGemma 3 questions (valid? derived? rephrase?) and retries
  - Consent entities explicitly skipped (not groundable to codes)
  - Concurrency control: semaphore(4) + asyncio.gather for parallel entity processing
  - Demographics handled via agentic routing (age/gender reasoning)
  - Expert review routing on exhausted attempts

#### 5. **persist.py**
- **Purpose**: Fifth node. Creates Entity records and updates protocol status to 'pending_review' or 'grounding_failed'.
- **Key Functions**:
  - `persist_node()` - main handler
  - `_create_entity_record()` - maps grounding result to Entity DB record
  - `_find_criterion_and_update_mappings()` - updates field_mappings in Criteria.conditions JSONB
  - `_update_batch_and_protocol()` - updates batch status and protocol status
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - Partial success: some entities succeeded + some failed → 'pending_review'
  - Total failure (ALL entities failed) → 'grounding_failed'
  - Field mappings accumulated (extended, not overwritten)
  - Criterion ID threading from parse → ground → persist for direct lookup
  - Review inheritance support for re-extraction runs
  - Protocol status audit logging on transition

#### 6. **ordinal_resolve.py**
- **Purpose**: Seventh node (after structure). Identifies unrecognized ordinal scales and updates unit_concept_id to 8527.
- **Key Functions**:
  - `ordinal_resolve_node()` - main handler
  - `_query_candidates()` - finds AtomicCriterion records with null unit_concept_id + non-null value_numeric + null unit_text
  - `_deduplicate_candidates()` - dedupes by entity text
  - `_process_batch()` - sends candidates to Gemini for ordinal identification
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - Queries records with specific null/non-null patterns (strong signal for ordinals)
  - Error accumulation: LLM failures don't block pipeline
  - AuditLog proposals for human review
  - Returns proposals_json for later review

---

### **Event System (events-py library)**

#### 7. **outbox.py**
- **Purpose**: Implements transactional outbox pattern for publishing domain events with at-least-once delivery.
- **Key Classes**:
  - `OutboxProcessor` - polls OutboxEvent table, dispatches to registered handlers
  - `persist_with_outbox()` - helper to persist entity + outbox event in single transaction
- **Key Functions**:
  - `poll_and_process()` - polls pending/failed events, executes handlers, marks as published or dead_letter
  - `start()` / `stop()` - async control
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - Max retries (3) before marking dead_letter
  - PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED for concurrent safety
  - Protocol status updated to dead_letter on event exhaustion
  - Context variable copying to preserve MLflow tracing
  - Dedicated ThreadPoolExecutor to avoid starving FastAPI handlers

#### 8. **models.py**
- **Purpose**: Event envelope and domain event kind definitions.
- **Key Classes**:
  - `EventKind` - enum: CREATED, UPDATED, DELETED
  - `DomainEventKind` - enum: PROTOCOL_UPLOADED, CRITERIA_EXTRACTED, REVIEW_COMPLETED, ENTITIES_GROUNDED
  - `EventEnvelope` - TypedDict for basic events
  - `DomainEventEnvelope` - TypedDict for outbox pattern events
- **Key Functions**:
  - `create_event()` - creates basic event envelope
  - `create_domain_event()` - creates domain event with idempotency key

---

### **API Service - Exports**

#### 9. **exports.py**
- **Purpose**: FastAPI endpoints for exporting protocol criteria in standard formats (CIRCE, FHIR Group, evaluation SQL).
- **Key Functions**:
  - `export_circe()` - exports as OHDSI CIRCE CohortExpression JSON
  - `export_fhir_group()` - exports as FHIR R4 Group resource
  - `export_evaluation_sql()` - exports as OMOP CDM evaluation SQL
  - `_get_export_data_or_404()` - loads export data or raises 404
  - `_make_stats()` - builds ExportStats (criteria_count, atomic_count, composite_count, relationship_count)
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - Depends on `load_protocol_export_data()` from exporters.__init__
  - Response models with nested stats
  - PlainTextResponse for SQL output

#### 10. **exporters/__init__.py**
- **Purpose**: Shared data loader for protocol export builders. Loads all structured criteria data into a single dataclass.
- **Key Classes**:
  - `ProtocolExportData` - dataclass holding protocol, criteria, atomics, composites, relationships + lookup dicts
- **Key Functions**:
  - `load_protocol_export_data()` - queries protocol, active batch, criteria, atomics, composites, relationships
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - Filters to active (non-archived) batch
  - Early returns (None) if protocol/batch/criteria missing
  - Builds atomics_by_id and criteria_by_id lookup dicts for exporters
  - Queries composites and relationships separately

  - Pipeline: LangChain, LangGraph, Transformers, Torch
  - APIs: google-genai, google-cloud-aiplatform, vertexai
  - NLP: sentence-transformers, tooluniverse
  - Utilities: aiohttp, httpx, requests, tenacity, alembic, pymupdf
- **Notable Patterns**:
  - uv workspace with 8 member packages (services + libs)
  - Python 3.12+ requirement
  - Dev dependencies: mypy, pytest, pytest-asyncio, ruff, mlflow
  - Pytest async mode auto
  - Parallel test execution (-n auto)

---

### **Test Coverage**

**Test Files Found** (10 files in services/api-service/tests):
- `test_auth_required.py` - authentication
- `test_protocol_api.py` - protocol endpoints
- `test_review_api.py` - review workflows
- `test_exports.py` - export endpoints
- `test_umls_clients.py` - UMLS integration
- `test_models.py`, `test_schemas.py`, `test_quality.py`, `test_integrity.py` - data validation
- `conftest.py` - fixtures

**No HITL UI tests found** - apps/hitl-ui/src/**/*.test.* returned no results.

---

## Architecture Patterns Summary

1. **Pipeline Pattern**: 7-node LangGraph pipeline (ingest→extract→parse→ground→persist→structure→ordinal_resolve)
2. **Thin Orchestration**: Node files delegate logic to tools, keep state mutations minimal
3. **Error Accumulation**: Individual entity/criterion failures logged but don't crash pipeline
4. **Dual Sourcing**: Entities grounded via both TerminologyRouter + OMOP mapper, results reconciled
5. **Agentic Retry Loop**: Low-confidence groundings trigger up to 3 retry attempts with MedGemma reasoning
6. **Transactional Outbox**: Domain events written with entities in single DB transaction for at-least-once delivery
7. **State Size Optimization**: Clears large objects (pdf_bytes) after use; passes JSON strings not dicts
8. **Concurrency Control**: Semaphores limit parallel API calls; asyncio.gather for batching
9. **Audit Trail**: All decisions (grounding, status changes) logged to AuditLog table
10. **Cross-Service Integration**: Graph nodes intentionally import from api-service for DB access during orchestration

{
  "file_path": "/Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/scripts/generate_components_overview.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Generate docs/components/index.md from workspace member directories.\n\nScans services/, libs/, and apps/ for component directories and writes\na summary page with links to each component's docs (if present).\n\nCalled by: make docs-components-gen\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nDOCS_DIR = ROOT / \"docs\" / \"components\"\n\nCOMPONENT_DIRS = [\n    (\"Services\", ROOT / \"services\"),\n    (\"Libraries\", ROOT / \"libs\"),\n    (\"Applications\", ROOT / \"apps\"),\n]\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    DOCS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    out = DOCS_DIR / \"index.md\"\n\n    lines: list[str] = [\n        \"# Components Overview\",\n        \"\",\n        \"Auto-generated list of workspace components.\",\n        \"\",\n    ]\n\n    for section_name, base_dir in COMPONENT_DIRS:\n        if not base_dir.is_dir():\n            continue\n        children = sorted(\n            p for p in base_dir.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and not p.name.startswith(\".\")\n        )\n        if not children:\n            continue\n\n        lines.append(f\"## {section_name}\")\n        lines.append(\"\")\n        lines.append(\"| Component | Has Docs | pyproject.toml |\")\n        lines.append(\"|-----------|----------|----------------|\")\n\n        for child in children:\n            has_docs = (child / \"docs\").is_dir()\n            has_pyproj = (child / \"pyproject.toml\").is_file()\n            has_pkg = (child / \"package.json\").is_file()\n            config = \"yes\" if (has_pyproj or has_pkg) else \"no\"\n            docs_status = \"yes\" if has_docs else \"no\"\n            rel = os.path.relpath(child, ROOT)\n            lines.append(f\"| `{rel}` | {docs_status} | {config} |\")\n\n        lines.append(\"\")\n\n    out.write_text(\"\\n\".join(lines) + \"\\n\")\n    print(f\"Generated {out}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

{

  "content": "\"\"\"Validate root mkdocs.yml navigation references.\n\nChecks that all markdown files referenced in mkdocs.yml nav actually exist\nin the docs/ directory. Prints warnings for missing files. Does NOT modify\nmkdocs.yml — the nav is hand-maintained.\n\nCalled by: make docs-nav-update\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\nDOCS_DIR = ROOT / \"docs\"\nMKDOCS_YML = ROOT / \"mkdocs.yml\"\n\n\ndef main() -> None:\n    content = MKDOCS_YML.read_text()\n\n    # Extract .md file references from nav (simple regex — not a full YAML parse)\n    md_refs = re.findall(r\":\\s+([^\\s!][^\\n]*\\.md)\", content)\n\n    missing = []\n    for ref in md_refs:\n        ref = ref.strip()\n        path = DOCS_DIR / ref\n        if not path.exists():\n            missing.append(ref)\n\n    if missing:\n        print(f\"WARNING: {len(missing)} nav reference(s) have no file yet:\")\n        for m in missing:\n            print(f\"  - docs/{m}\")\n    else:\n        print(\"All nav references resolve to existing files.\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

  "command": "cat > /Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/docs/index.md << 'DOCEOF'\n# ElixirTrials\n\nAI-powered extraction and structuring of clinical trial eligibility criteria from protocol PDFs.\n\n## What is ElixirTrials?\n\nElixirTrials takes a clinical trial protocol PDF and produces structured, coded eligibility criteria ready for cohort identification. The system combines:\n\n- **Gemini-powered extraction** — LLM reads the PDF and extracts inclusion/exclusion criteria\n- **Multi-terminology grounding** — entities are linked to SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, ICD-10 via UMLS + OMOP\n- **Expression tree structuring** — criteria are decomposed into atomic conditions with AND/OR/NOT logic\n- **Human-in-the-loop review** — clinicians review, approve, or modify AI-generated criteria\n- **Standard exports** — output in OHDSI CIRCE, FHIR R4 Group, and OMOP CDM evaluation SQL\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```bash\n# 1. Clone and configure\ncp .env.example .env    # Fill in GOOGLE_API_KEY, UMLS_API_KEY, etc.\n\n# 2. Start everything\nmake run-dev            # Starts DB + MLflow + API + UI\n\n# 3. Open the UI\nopen http://localhost:3000\n```\n\n## Architecture at a Glance\n\n```mermaid\ngraph LR\n    UI[hitl-ui<br/>React + Vite] -->|HTTP| API[api-service<br/>FastAPI]\n    API -->|outbox event| PP[protocol-processor-service<br/>LangGraph]\n    API --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]\n    PP --> DB\n    PP -->|Gemini API| LLM[Gemini 2.5 Flash]\n    PP -->|UMLS + OMOP| VOCAB[Terminology Services]\n    API --> MLflow[MLflow]\n```\n\n## Documentation Map\n\n| Section | What you'll find |\n|---------|-----------------|\n| [Onboarding](onboarding.md) | First-time setup, prerequisites, environment configuration |\n| [Architecture](architecture/index.md) | System design, data models, service boundaries |\n| [User Journeys](journeys/index.md) | End-to-end workflows with sequence diagrams |\n| [Components](components/index.md) | Per-service deep dives with file paths |\n| [Diagrams](diagrams/hitl-flow.md) | Visual reference for HITL, agent, and pipeline flows |\n| [Code Tour](code-tour/index.md) | Slide-style walkthrough of key code paths |\n| [Status](status/index.md) | What's production-ready vs experimental |\n| [Guides](testing-guide.md) | Testing, auth setup, development guides |\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created index.md\"",

Clone and Install\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/noahdolevelixir/medgemma-hackathon.git\ncd medgemma-hackathon\nuv sync                    # Install all Python dependencies\ncd apps/hitl-ui && npm install && cd ../..\n```\n\n## 2. Environment Configuration\n\n```bash\ncp .env.example .env\n```\n\nEdit `.env` with your credentials:\n\n| Variable | Required | Source |\n|----------|----------|--------|\n| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Yes | [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey) |\n| `UMLS_API_KEY` | Yes | [UMLS Sign Up](https://uts.nlm.nih.gov/uts/signup-login) |\n| `GEMINI_MODEL_NAME` | No | Defaults to `gemini-2.5-flash` |\n| `MODEL_BACKEND` | No | `vertex` for Vertex AI, omit for Gemini Developer API |\n| `GCP_PROJECT_ID` | If Vertex | Your GCP project ID |\n| `GCP_REGION` | If Vertex | e.g., `europe-west4` |\n| `VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID` | If Vertex | MedGemma endpoint ID |\n| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | No | OAuth login (dev works without) |\n| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | No | OAuth login (dev works without) |\n| `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` | No | Defaults to `http://localhost:5001` |\n\n## 3. Start the Dev Stack\n\n```bash\nmake run-dev\n```\n\nThis starts:\n\n- **PostgreSQL** on port 5432 (Docker)\n- **MLflow** on port 5001 (local)\n- **API service** on port 8000 (uvicorn with hot-reload)\n- **UI** on port 3000 (Vite dev server)\n\nAlternatively, start components individually:\n\n```bash\nmake run-infra    # DB + MLflow only\nmake run-api      # API service only\nmake run-ui       # UI only\n```\n\n## 4. Verify\n\n1. Open [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) — you should see the HITL UI\n2. Check [http://localhost:8000/health](http://localhost:8000/health) — should return `{\"status\": \"healthy\"}`\n3. Check [http://localhost:5001](http://localhost:5001) — MLflow dashboard\n\n## 5. Upload a Protocol\n\n1. Click **Upload Protocol** in the UI\n2. Drop a clinical trial protocol PDF (max 50 MB)\n3. The pipeline runs automatically: extract → parse → ground → structure\n4. Review extracted criteria in the HITL review page\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\nmedgemma-hackathon/\n├── apps/hitl-ui/              # React + Vite frontend\n├── services/\n│   ├── api-service/           # FastAPI backend (REST + outbox)\n│   └── protocol-processor-service/  # LangGraph pipeline\n├── libs/\n│   ├── shared/                # SQLModel data models\n│   ├── events-py/             # Outbox processor + event contracts\n│   ├── inference/             # Model inference utilities\n│   ├── evaluation/            # Quality evaluation\n│   ├── data-pipeline/         # Data loading utilities\n│   └── model-training/        # Fine-tuning scripts\n├── infra/                     # Docker Compose, OMOP vocab\n├── scripts/                   # Dev tooling, migrations\n├── docs/                      # This documentation\n├── Makefile                   # All dev commands\n└── mkdocs.yml                 # Docs site config\n```\n\n## Common Commands\n\n```bash\nmake help          # Show all available commands\nmake check         # Run linters + type checkers + tests\nmake lint-fix      # Auto-fix lint issues\nmake test          # Run all tests\nmake docs-build    # Build documentation site\nmake docs-serve    # Serve docs at http://localhost:8000\n```\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created onboarding.md\"",

{
  "command": "cat > /Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/docs/architecture/index.md << 'DOCEOF'\n# Architecture Overview\n\nElixirTrials is a monorepo containing three runtime components and several shared libraries, all orchestrated through an event-driven pipeline.\n\n## Core Principles\n\n1. **Consolidated pipeline** — All processing (extraction, grounding, structuring) runs in a single `protocol-processor-service` via LangGraph. The earlier two-service split (`extraction-service` + `grounding-service`) is legacy.\n2. **Event-driven trigger** — Processing starts from a `protocol_uploaded` outbox event. There is no `criteria_extracted` cross-service event.\n3. **Error accumulation** — Individual entity/criterion failures don't crash the pipeline. Partial results are preserved alongside errors.\n4. **Human-in-the-loop** — All AI outputs go through a review step before being considered final.\n\n## Runtime Components\n\n| Component | Tech | Port | Role |\n|-----------|------|------|------|\n| `hitl-ui` | React + Vite + Radix | 3000 | Upload PDFs, review criteria, manage protocols |\n| `api-service` | FastAPI + SQLModel | 8000 | REST API, outbox processor, export endpoints |\n| `protocol-processor-service` | LangGraph + Gemini | (in-process) | 7-node extraction/grounding/structuring pipeline |\n\n## Shared Libraries\n\n| Library | Purpose |\n|---------|---------|\n| `libs/shared` | SQLModel domain models (`Protocol`, `Criteria`, `Entity`, etc.) |\n| `libs/events-py` | Transactional outbox processor and domain event contracts |\n| `libs/inference` | Model inference utilities |\n| `libs/evaluation` | Quality evaluation framework |\n| `libs/data-pipeline` | Data loading helpers |\n| `libs/model-training` | Fine-tuning scripts |\n\n## Infrastructure\n\n| Service | Tech | Purpose |\n|---------|------|---------|\n| PostgreSQL | 16-alpine | Application database + LangGraph checkpoints |\n| MLflow | v3.9.0 | Experiment tracking, trace observability |\n| OMOP Vocab DB | PostgreSQL | Optional OMOP vocabulary for concept resolution |\n| Pub/Sub Emulator | GCP emulator | Not actively used (outbox pattern preferred) |\n\nSee [System Architecture](system-architecture.md) for diagrams and [Data Models](data-models.md) for the schema.\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created architecture/index.md\"",
  "description": "Create docs/architecture/index.md"
}

{
  "command": "cat > /Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/docs/architecture/system-architecture.md << 'DOCEOF'\n# System Architecture\n\n## Container Diagram\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TB\n    subgraph \"Browser\"\n        UI[\"hitl-ui<br/>(React + Vite + Radix UI)\"]\n    end\n\n    subgraph \"Backend\"\n        API[\"api-service<br/>(FastAPI + SQLModel)\"]\n        OBX[\"OutboxProcessor<br/>(events-py)\"]\n        PP[\"protocol-processor-service<br/>(LangGraph StateGraph)\"]\n    end\n\n    subgraph \"Infrastructure\"\n        DB[(PostgreSQL 16)]\n        MLF[\"MLflow v3.9\"]\n        OMOP[(OMOP Vocab DB<br/>optional)]\n    end\n\n    subgraph \"External Services\"\n        GEMINI[\"Gemini 2.5 Flash<br/>(Google AI / Vertex AI)\"]\n        UMLS[\"UMLS API<br/>(NLM)\"]\n        GCS[\"GCS / Local Storage\"]\n    end\n\n    UI -->|\"HTTP REST\"| API\n    API --> DB\n    API --> OBX\n    OBX -->|\"protocol_uploaded\"| PP\n    PP --> DB\n    PP -->|\"PDF extraction\"| GEMINI\n    PP -->|\"Entity grounding\"| UMLS\n    PP -->|\"Concept resolution\"| OMOP\n    PP -->|\"PDF fetch\"| GCS\n    API -->|\"Traces\"| MLF\n    PP -->|\"Traces\"| MLF\n```\n\n## Communication Paths\n\n### Synchronous HTTP (UI to API)\n\nAll UI interactions flow through the FastAPI REST API:\n\n| Path | Description | Key file |\n|------|-------------|----------|\n| `POST /protocols/upload` | Generate signed upload URL | `services/api-service/src/api_service/protocols.py` |\n| `POST /protocols/{id}/confirm-upload` | Confirm upload, trigger pipeline | `protocols.py` |\n| `GET /protocols` | List protocols (paginated) | `protocols.py` |\n| `GET /reviews/batches/{id}/criteria` | Fetch criteria for review | `reviews.py` |\n| `POST /reviews/criteria/{id}/action` | Submit review decision | `reviews.py` |\n| `GET /exports/{id}/circe` | Export as CIRCE JSON | `exports.py` |\n| `GET /exports/{id}/fhir-group` | Export as FHIR R4 Group | `exports.py` |\n| `GET /exports/{id}/evaluation-sql` | Export as OMOP SQL | `exports.py` |\n\n### Asynchronous Event Processing (Outbox to Pipeline)\n\nThe pipeline is triggered via the transactional outbox pattern:\n\n1. `confirm-upload` endpoint calls `persist_with_outbox()` — writes `Protocol` record + `OutboxEvent` in a single DB transaction\n2. `OutboxProcessor` polls the `outboxevent` table every 2 seconds\n3. When it finds a `protocol_uploaded` event, it calls `handle_protocol_uploaded()` in a thread executor\n4. The handler invokes the 7-node LangGraph pipeline via `asyncio.run()`\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n    participant UI as hitl-ui\n    participant API as api-service\n    participant DB as PostgreSQL\n    participant OBX as OutboxProcessor\n    participant PP as protocol-processor\n\n    UI->>API: POST /protocols/{id}/confirm-upload\n    API->>DB: INSERT Protocol + OutboxEvent (single tx)\n    API-->>UI: 200 OK\n\n    loop Every 2s\n        OBX->>DB: SELECT FROM outboxevent WHERE status='pending'\n    end\n    OBX->>PP: handle_protocol_uploaded(payload)\n    PP->>DB: UPDATE protocol.status = 'extracting'\n    PP->>PP: Run 7-node LangGraph pipeline\n    PP->>DB: INSERT criteria, entities, atomics\n    PP->>DB: UPDATE protocol.status = 'pending_review'\n```\n\n### Storage Paths\n\n- **Local dev**: Files stored in `./uploads/` directory, served by `api-service` at `/local-files/{path}`\n- **Production**: Files uploaded to GCS via signed URL, fetched by pipeline from `gs://` URI\n\n### Observability\n\n- **MLflow**: Traces emitted by both `api-service` (request middleware) and pipeline nodes (per-node spans)\n- **Tracking URI**: `http://localhost:5001` (local), `http://mlflow:5000` (Docker)\n- **Experiment**: `protocol-processing`\n- **Orphan cleanup**: `trigger.py` closes stale IN_PROGRESS traces at startup\n\n## Authentication\n\n- **Google OAuth 2.0** via `api-service/auth.py`\n- Session middleware with JWT tokens\n- All API routes (except `/auth/*` and `/health`) require authentication\n- Dev mode works without OAuth configured\n\n## Error Handling\n\n| Error type | Behavior | Status |\n|------------|----------|--------|\n| Fatal (PDF corrupt, auth fail) | Pipeline stops at failed node | `extraction_failed` |\n| Partial (some entities fail grounding) | Pipeline continues, errors accumulated | `pending_review` with `errors[]` |\n| Total grounding failure | All entities failed | `grounding_failed` |\n| Outbox exhaustion (3 retries) | Event marked dead_letter | `dead_letter` |\n| Dead letter aging (7+ days) | Lazy archival on next access | `archived` |\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created architecture/system-architecture.md\"",
  "description": "Create docs/architecture/system-architecture.md"
}
```

{
  "command": "cat > /Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/docs/architecture/data-models.md << 'DOCEOF'\n# Data Models\n\nAll domain models live in `libs/shared/src/shared/models.py` using SQLModel (SQLAlchemy + Pydantic).\n\n## Entity-Relationship Overview\n\n```mermaid\nerDiagram\n    Protocol ||--o{ CriteriaBatch : \"has batches\"\n    CriteriaBatch ||--o{ Criteria : \"contains\"\n    Criteria ||--o{ Entity : \"has entities\"\n    Criteria ||--o{ AtomicCriterion : \"decomposes to\"\n    Criteria ||--o{ CompositeCriterion : \"groups via\"\n    CompositeCriterion ||--o{ CriterionRelationship : \"parent\"\n    Protocol ||--o{ AtomicCriterion : \"belongs to\"\n    Protocol ||--o{ CompositeCriterion : \"belongs to\"\n    Review }o--|| Criteria : \"reviews\"\n    Review }o--|| Entity : \"reviews\"\n    OutboxEvent }o--|| Protocol : \"triggers for\"\n```\n\n## Core Tables\n\n### Protocol\n\nUploaded clinical trial protocol PDF. Central aggregate root.\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|--------|------|-------------|\n| `id` | UUID (str) | Primary key |\n| `title` | str | From filename or user input |\n| `file_uri` | str | GCS URI (`gs://...`) or local path (`local://...`) |\n| `status` | str | Current processing state (see lifecycle below) |\n| `page_count` | int? | PDF page count from quality analysis |\n| `quality_score` | float? | 0-1 score from PDF quality check |\n| `error_reason` | str? | Human-readable failure message |\n| `metadata_` | JSON | Quality details, pipeline_thread_id, error info |\n\n**File**: `libs/shared/src/shared/models.py:59`\n\n### Protocol Status Lifecycle\n\n```mermaid\nstateDiagram-v2\n    [*] --> uploaded: POST /upload\n    uploaded --> extracting: confirm-upload (outbox)\n    extracting --> extraction_failed: Fatal error\n    extracting --> grounding: Pipeline progress\n    grounding --> grounding_failed: All entities fail\n    grounding --> pending_review: Pipeline success\n    pending_review --> complete: All criteria reviewed\n    extraction_failed --> extracting: retry / re-extract\n    grounding_failed --> extracting: retry / re-extract\n    extraction_failed --> dead_letter: Outbox exhausted (3 retries)\n    dead_letter --> archived: Lazy archival (7+ days)\n    extraction_failed --> archived: Manual archive\n    grounding_failed --> archived: Manual archive\n    dead_letter --> extracting: retry\n```\n\n### CriteriaBatch\n\nA batch of criteria extracted from a protocol. Re-extraction creates a new batch and archives old ones.\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|--------|------|-------------|\n| `id` | UUID (str) | Primary key |\n| `protocol_id` | FK → Protocol | Parent protocol |\n| `status` | str | Batch review status |\n| `extraction_model` | str? | Model used for extraction |\n| `is_archived` | bool | Hidden from dashboard when True |\n\n**File**: `libs/shared/src/shared/models.py:74`\n\n### Criteria\n\nIndividual inclusion/exclusion criterion extracted from a protocol.\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|--------|------|-------------|\n| `id` | UUID (str) | Primary key |\n| `batch_id` | FK → CriteriaBatch | Parent batch |\n| `criteria_type` | str | `inclusion` or `exclusion` |\n| `text` | text | Original criterion text |\n| `structured_criterion` | JSON? | Expression tree (Phase 2) |\n| `conditions` | JSON? | Contains `field_mappings` from grounding |\n| `confidence` | float | Extraction confidence (0-1) |\n| `review_status` | str? | Human review decision |\n\n**File**: `libs/shared/src/shared/models.py:86`\n\n### Entity\n\nMedical entity extracted from a criterion (e.g., \"Type 2 diabetes\", \"HbA1c\").\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|--------|------|-------------|\n| `id` | UUID (str) | Primary key |\n| `criteria_id` | FK → Criteria | Parent criterion |\n| `entity_type` | str | `condition`, `measurement`, `drug`, etc. |\n| `text` | str | Entity surface text |\n| `snomed_code` | str? | SNOMED CT code |\n| `rxnorm_code` | str? | RxNorm code |\n| `loinc_code` | str? | LOINC code |\n| `icd10_code` | str? | ICD-10 code |\n| `omop_concept_id` | str? | OMOP CDM concept ID |\n\n**File**: `libs/shared/src/shared/models.py:114`\n\n### AtomicCriterion\n\nLeaf node in an expression tree. Represents a single testable condition (e.g., \"HbA1c >= 7%\").\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|--------|------|-------------|\n| `id` | UUID (str) | Primary key |\n| `criterion_id` | FK → Criteria | Parent criterion |\n| `protocol_id` | FK → Protocol | Owning protocol |\n| `inclusion_exclusion` | str | `inclusion` or `exclusion` |\n| `entity_domain` | str? | `condition`, `measurement`, `drug`, `demographics`, etc. |\n| `omop_concept_id` | str? | OMOP concept ID for CDM joins |\n| `entity_concept_id` | str? | Source terminology code |\n| `entity_concept_system` | str? | `snomed`, `loinc`, `rxnorm` |\n| `relation_operator` | str? | `>=`, `<=`, `=`, `>`, `<`, `!=` |\n| `value_numeric` | float? | Numeric threshold |\n| `value_text` | str? | Text value (e.g., \"Class III-IV\") |\n| `unit_text` | str? | Unit label |\n| `unit_concept_id` | int? | OMOP unit concept ID |\n| `negation` | bool | True for negated conditions |\n\n**File**: `libs/shared/src/shared/models.py:184`  \n**Table**: `atomic_criteria`\n\n### CompositeCriterion\n\nBranch node in an expression tree. Combines children with AND/OR/NOT logic.\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|--------|------|-------------|\n| `id` | UUID (str) | Primary key |\n| `criterion_id` | FK → Criteria | Parent criterion |\n| `protocol_id` | FK → Protocol | Owning protocol |\n| `logic_operator` | str | `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` |\n\n**File**: `libs/shared/src/shared/models.py:235`  \n**Table**: `composite_criteria`\n\n### CriterionRelationship\n\nEdge in the expression tree. Links parent composite to child (atomic or composite).\n\n| Column | Type | Description |\n|--------|------|-------------|\n| `parent_criterion_id` | FK → CompositeCriterion | Parent (PK) |\n| `child_criterion_id` | str | Child ID (PK) |\n| `child_type` | str | `atomic` or `composite` |\n| `child_sequence` | int | Operand ordering |\n\n**File**: `libs/shared/src/shared/models.py:263`  \n**Table**: `criterion_relationships`\n\n### Supporting Tables\n\n| Table | Purpose | File line |\n|-------|---------|-----------|\n| `review` | Human review actions with before/after JSON | `models.py:144` |\n| `auditlog` | Immutable log of all system events | `models.py:158` |\n| `user` | Authenticated user accounts (Google OAuth) | `models.py:170` |\n| `outboxevent` | Transactional outbox for event publishing | `models.py:285` |\n\n## Pipeline State\n\nThe LangGraph pipeline passes state between nodes as a `PipelineState` TypedDict.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/state.py`\n\n| Field | Type | Set by |\n|-------|------|--------|\n| `protocol_id` | str | Input (always present) |\n| `file_uri` | str | Input |\n| `title` | str | Input |\n| `batch_id` | str? | parse node |\n| `pdf_bytes` | bytes? | ingest node (cleared after extract) |\n| `extraction_json` | str? | extract node |\n| `entities_json` | str? | parse node |\n| `grounded_entities_json` | str? | ground node |\n| `archived_reviewed_criteria` | list? | Input (re-extraction only) |\n| `ordinal_proposals_json` | str? | ordinal_resolve node |\n| `status` | str | Each node |\n| `error` | str? | Fatal errors → routes to END |\n| `errors` | list[str] | Accumulated non-fatal errors |\n\nState is serialized as JSON strings (not dicts) between nodes to minimize LangGraph checkpoint size.\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created architecture/data-models.md\"",

Upload Dialog (`ProtocolUploadDialog.tsx`)\n\nThe user opens the upload dialog in the HITL UI. Client-side validation enforces:\n\n- PDF content type only\n- 50 MB maximum file size\n\n**File**: `apps/hitl-ui/src/components/ProtocolUploadDialog.tsx`\n\n### 2. Signed URL Generation (`protocols.py`)\n\nThe API creates a `Protocol` record (status: `uploaded`) and returns a signed URL for direct browser-to-GCS upload. If the Gemini circuit breaker is open, the protocol is marked `pending` with a warning.\n\n**File**: `services/api-service/src/api_service/protocols.py:136`\n\n### 3. Upload Confirmation (`protocols.py`)\n\nAfter the browser uploads the file, it calls `confirm-upload`. This endpoint:\n\n1. Optionally decodes `pdf_bytes_base64` and computes a quality score (page count, text extractability)\n2. Stores quality metadata on the GCS blob\n3. Writes the `PROTOCOL_UPLOADED` outbox event in the same transaction as the protocol update\n\n**File**: `services/api-service/src/api_service/protocols.py:205`\n\n### 4. Outbox Processing (`events-py/outbox.py`)\n\nThe `OutboxProcessor` runs as a background task inside `api-service`. It polls for pending events and dispatches them to registered handlers in a thread executor (to avoid blocking FastAPI).\n\n**File**: `libs/events-py/src/events_py/outbox.py`\n\n### 5. Ingest Node (`nodes/ingest.py`)\n\nFirst pipeline node. Fetches the raw PDF bytes from GCS (or local storage) and updates the protocol status to `extracting`.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/ingest.py`\n\n### 6. Extract Node (`nodes/extract.py`)\n\nSends the PDF to Gemini 2.5 Flash with a structured output schema requesting:\n\n- Criteria text (inclusion/exclusion)\n- Category classification\n- Confidence scores\n\nReturns a JSON string of extracted criteria. The PDF bytes are cleared from state after this step to reduce checkpoint size.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/extract.py`\n\n### 7. Parse Node (`nodes/parse.py`)\n\nConverts extraction JSON into database records:\n\n1. **Phase A**: Creates `CriteriaBatch` and `Criteria` records in the database\n2. **Phase B**: Runs `decompose_entities_from_criterion()` concurrently (asyncio.gather with semaphore=4) to identify medical entities within each criterion\n\nProduces `entities_json` in state for the grounding phase.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/parse.py`\n\n## Error Handling\n\n| Failure | Response |\n|---------|----------|\n| Invalid file type | 400 error at upload |\n| File too large (>50MB) | 400 error at upload |\n| PDF quality too low | Pipeline may fail at extract with `extraction_failed` |\n| Gemini API down | Circuit breaker opens; protocol queued as `pending` |\n| Extraction LLM error | `extraction_failed` status; retryable via `/retry` endpoint |\n\n## Re-Extraction\n\nThe `POST /protocols/{id}/re-extract` endpoint allows re-running extraction without re-uploading:\n\n1. Archives all existing non-archived batches (preserves review history)\n2. Collects reviewed criteria from archived batches for fuzzy-match inheritance\n3. Triggers the same pipeline via a new `PROTOCOL_UPLOADED` outbox event\n4. New batch criteria inherit review decisions from archived criteria (>90% text match, same type)\n\n**File**: `services/api-service/src/api_service/protocols.py:360`\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created journeys/upload-extraction.md\"",

standard terminologies, structured into expression trees, and reviewed by clinicians.\n\n## Sequence Diagram\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n    participant PA as parse node\n    participant GR as ground node\n    participant UMLS as UMLS API\n    participant OMOP as OMOP Mapper\n    participant PE as persist node\n    participant ST as structure node\n    participant OR as ordinal_resolve ST->>DB: SELECT criteria with field_mappings\n    loop For each criterion (semaphore=4)\n        ST->>ST: Gemini detect_logic_structure()\n        ST->>DB: INSERT AtomicCriterion + CompositeCriterion\n        ST->>DB: INSERT CriterionRelationship edges\n        ST->>DB: UPDATE Criteria.structured_criterion (JSON tree)\n    end\n\n    ST->>OR: state\n    OR->>DB: SELECT atomics with null unit_concept_id\n    OR->>OR: Gemini ordinal scale detection\n    OR->>DB: UPDATE unit_concept_id = 8527 (ordinal)\n    OR->>DB: INSERT AuditLog proposals\n\n    Note over DB,UI: Protocol now in pending_review\n    Clinician->>UI: Open Review Page\n    UI->>DB: GET /reviews/batches/{id}/criteria\n    UI-->>Clinician: Show criteria split by inclusion/exclusion\n\n    loop For each criterion\n        Clinician->>UI: Approve / Reject / Modify\n        UI->>DB: POST /reviews/criteria/{id}/action\n    end\n```\n\n## Grounding Phase (ground node)\n\nThe ground node processes each entity through a dual-grounding pipeline:\n\n### Dual Grounding\n\n1. **TerminologyRouter** — routes entities to the appropriate UMLS source vocabulary (SNOMED for conditions, LOINC for labs, RxNorm for drugs)\n2. **OMOP Mapper** — resolves entities to OMOP CDM concept IDs for data warehouse joins\n\nBoth run in parallel per entity (asyncio.gather), results reconciled in `_reconcile_dual_grounding()`.\n\n### Agentic Retry Loop\n\nWhen initial grounding confidence is below 0.5, the ground node enters an agentic reasoning loop (max 3 attempts):\n\n1. Asks MedGemma: \"Is this entity valid for coding?\"\n2. Asks: \"Can we derive a parent/broader concept?\"\n3. Asks: \"Can you rephrase for better matching?\"\n4. Retries grounding with improved input\n\nIf all attempts fail, the entity is marked for expert review.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/ground.py`\n\n### Error Accumulation\n\nIndividual entity failures are collected in `state[\"errors\"]` but don't stop the pipeline. The persist node decides the final status:\n\n- All entities succeed → `pending_review`\n- Some entities fail → `pending_review` (with errors logged)\n- All entities fail → `grounding_failed`\n\n## Persist Phase (persist node)\n\nCreates `Entity` records in the database and updates `Criteria.conditions.field_mappings` with grounding results. Also handles review inheritance during re-extraction.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/persist.py`\n\n## Structure Phase (structure node)\n\nBuilds expression trees for criteria that have `field_mappings` in their conditions JSON:\n\n1. Queries criteria from the current batch\n2. For each qualifying criterion, calls Gemini to detect logic structure (AND/OR/NOT)\n3. Creates `AtomicCriterion` leaf records with OMOP concept IDs, operators, values\n4. Creates `CompositeCriterion` branch records with logic operators\n5. Creates `CriterionRelationship` edges linking parents to children\n6. Stores the expression tree as `structured_criterion` JSON on the Criteria record\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/structure.py`\n\n### Expression Tree Example\n\nFor the criterion \"HbA1c between 7.0% and 10.0%\":\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"AND\",\n  \"children\": [\n    {\n      \"type\": \"ATOMIC\",\n      \"atomic_criterion_id\": \"uuid-1\",\n      \"details\": \"HbA1c >= 7.0%\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"type\": \"ATOMIC\",\n      \"atomic_criterion_id\": \"uuid-2\",\n      \"details\": \"HbA1c <= 10.0%\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThis maps to:\n\n- 1 `CompositeCriterion` (operator=AND)\n- 2 `AtomicCriterion` records (one for each bound)\n- 2 `CriterionRelationship` edges\n\n## Ordinal Resolution Phase (ordinal_resolve node)\n\nIdentifies atomic criteria that represent ordinal scales (e.g., NYHA class, ECOG score) and sets their `unit_concept_id` to 8527 (OMOP concept for ordinal).\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/ordinal_resolve.py`\n\n## HITL Review (ReviewPage.tsx)\n\nThe clinician reviews extracted criteria in a split-pane view:\n\n- **Left panel**: PDF viewer (highlights source text for selected criterion)\n- **Right panel**: Criteria list grouped by inclusion/exclusion, with filters for status, type, and confidence\n\nFor each criterion, the clinician can:\n\n- **Approve** — confirms the AI extraction is correct\n- **Reject** — marks as incorrect\n- **Modify** — provides corrections\n\nReview decisions are stored as `Review` records with before/after JSON for audit trail.\n\n**File**: `apps/hitl-ui/src/screens/ReviewPage.tsx`\n\n## Exports\n\nOnce criteria are reviewed, they can be exported in three formats:\n\n| Format | Endpoint | Use case |\n|--------|----------|----------|\n| CIRCE JSON | `GET /exports/{id}/circe` | OHDSI cohort definition tools (ATLAS) |\n| FHIR R4 Group | `GET /exports/{id}/fhir-group` | FHIR-based EHR systems |\n| OMOP SQL | `GET /exports/{id}/evaluation-sql` | Direct CDM database queries |\n\nAll export builders consume the same `ProtocolExportData` dataclass, which loads the expression tree (atomics, composites, relationships) from the database.\n\n**Files**:\n\n- `services/api-service/src/api_service/exports.py`\n- `services/api-service/src/api_service/exporters/circe_builder.py`\n- `services/api-service/src/api_service/exporters/fhir_group_builder.py`\n- `services/api-service/src/api_service/exporters/evaluation_sql_builder.py`\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created journeys/grounding-review.md\"",

Enables direct joins against CDM data warehouses.\n\n### Reconciliation\n\n`_reconcile_dual_grounding()` merges results from both paths:\n\n- Prefers OMOP concept ID when available (needed for exports)\n- Falls back to source terminology codes\n- Combines confidence scores from both paths\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/ground.py`\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created diagrams/agent-flow.md\"",

{
  "command": "cat > /Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/docs/diagrams/langgraph-architecture.md << 'DOCEOF'\n# LangGraph Pipeline Architecture\n\nThe protocol processing pipeline is implemented as a 7-node LangGraph StateGraph.\n\n## Pipeline Graph\n\n```mermaid\ngraph LR\n    START((START)) --> ingest\n    ingest -->|ok| extract\n    ingest -->|error| END1((END))\n    extract -->|ok| parse\n    extract -->|error| END2((END))\n    parse -->|ok| ground\n    parse -->|error| END3((END))\n    ground --> persist\n    persist --> structure\n    structure --> ordinal_resolve\n    ordinal_resolve --> END4((END))\n\n    style ingest fill:#3b82f6,color:#fff\n    style extract fill:#8b5cf6,color:#fff\n    style parse fill:#06b6d4,color:#fff\n    style ground fill:#10b981,color:#fff\n    style persist fill:#f59e0b,color:#fff\n    style structure fill:#ef4444,color:#fff\n    style ordinal_resolve fill:#ec4899,color:#fff\n```\n\n## Node Responsibilities\n\n| Node | Purpose | Key tool | Error strategy |\n|------|---------|----------|----------------|\n| **ingest** | Fetch PDF bytes from storage | `fetch_pdf_bytes()` | Fatal → END |\n| **extract** | LLM extraction of criteria from PDF | Gemini structured output | Fatal → END |\n| **parse** | Create DB records, decompose entities | `decompose_entities_from_criterion()` | Fatal → END |\n| **ground** | Link entities to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm/OMOP | TerminologyRouter + OMOP Mapper | Accumulate errors |\n| **persist** | Write Entity records, update field_mappings | Direct DB writes | Accumulate errors |\n| **structure** | Build expression trees from field_mappings | Gemini logic detection | Accumulate errors |\n| **ordinal_resolve** | Identify ordinal scales, set unit_concept_id | Gemini ordinal detection | Accumulate errors |\n\n## Error Routing\n\nThe first three nodes (ingest, extract, parse) use **conditional edges** — a fatal error routes to END immediately:\n\n```python\nworkflow.add_conditional_edges(\n    source,\n    should_continue,    # checks state[\"error\"]\n    {\"continue\": target, \"error\": END},\n)\n```\n\nThe remaining nodes (ground, persist, structure, ordinal_resolve) use **error accumulation** — individual item failures are appended to `state[\"errors\"]` but the pipeline continues.\n\n## Checkpointing\n\nThe graph is compiled with an `AsyncPostgresSaver` checkpointer that persists state after each node:\n\n- **Initial runs**: thread_id = `{protocol_id}:{uuid4}` (unique per run to prevent collision on re-extraction)\n- **Retry**: `retry_from_checkpoint(protocol_id)` looks up `pipeline_thread_id` from protocol metadata and resumes with `ainvoke(None, config)` — LangGraph replays from the last successful node\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/graph.py`\n\n## State Shape\n\nSee [Data Models — Pipeline State](../architecture/data-models.md#pipeline-state) for the full `PipelineState` TypedDict.\n\nKey design decisions:\n\n- **JSON strings** over dicts for extraction/entity data — reduces checkpoint serialization size\n- **pdf_bytes cleared** after extract — prevents storing megabytes in every checkpoint\n- **errors as list[str]** — simple accumulation, no structured error objects\nDOCEOF\necho `feature/major-refactor-langgraph` branch.\n\n## Maturity Matrix\n\n| Component | Status | Notes |\n|-----------|--------|-------|\n| PDF upload + quality scoring | Production-ready | Signed URL flow, client-side validation, quality analysis |\n| Gemini criteria extraction | Production-ready | Structured output with Gemini 2.5 Flash |\n| Entity decomposition (parse) | Production-ready | Concurrent async decomposition |\n| UMLS grounding (TerminologyRouter) | Production-ready | Multi-vocab routing with caching |\n| OMOP concept mapping | Production-ready | Dual grounding with reconciliation |\n| Agentic retry loop | Experimental | MedGemma reasoning for low-confidence entities |\n| Expression tree structuring | Production-ready | Gemini logic detection, atomic/composite model |\n| Ordinal scale resolution | Experimental | Gemini-based detection, proposals for review |\n| HITL review UI | Production-ready | Split-pane PDF + criteria, filtering, audit trail |\n| Re-extraction with review inheritance | Production-ready | Fuzzy matching (>90% threshold) |\n| CIRCE export | Production-ready | Full expression tree walking |\n| FHIR R4 Group export | Production-ready | Full expression tree walking |\n| OMOP evaluation SQL export | Production-ready (limited) | Flat AND/OR model only (see known limitations) |\n| LangGraph checkpointing | Production-ready | AsyncPostgresSaver with retry support |\n| Outbox event processing | Production-ready | At-least-once delivery, dead letter handling |\n| Google OAuth | Production-ready | JWT session with protected routes |\n| MLflow observability | Production-ready | Per-node traces, orphan cleanup |\n| Circuit breaker (Gemini) | Production-ready | pybreaker-based with UI warning |\n\n## Known Limitations\n\n### Evaluation SQL Builder (flat model)\n\nThe OMOP CDM evaluation SQL builder uses a flat AND/OR model: all inclusion atomics are combined with AND, all exclusion atomics use NOT EXISTS. The expression tree's nested AND/OR/NOT structure is **not** respected by the SQL builder.\n\nFor example, \"HbA1c >= 7% OR fasting glucose >= 126\" is evaluated as requiring **both** rather than **either**.\n\nThe CIRCE and FHIR Group builders correctly walk the expression tree.\n\n**File**: `services/api-service/src/api_service/exporters/evaluation_sql_builder.py:1-13`\n\n### CompositeCriterion.parent_criterion_id\n\nThe `parent_criterion_id` column on `CompositeCriterion` is intentionally unused by the automated pipeline. Tree parent-child relationships are stored in `CriterionRelationship`. This field is reserved for future HITL use (manual tree restructuring).\n\n### No UI Tests\n\nThe `apps/hitl-ui` directory has no test files. The React components are untested.\n\n### Stale Workspace Members\n\nSeveral workspace members in `pyproject.toml` exist as directories but have minimal functionality:\n\n- `libs/data-pipeline` — data loading helpers (limited)\n- `libs/evaluation` — quality evaluation framework (limited)\n- `libs/inference` — model inference utilities (limited)\n- `libs/model-training` — fine-tuning scripts (limited)\n\nThese are scaffolded for future use but not actively consumed by the pipeline.\n\n## Test Coverage\n\n| Area | Test files | Count | Runner |\n|------|-----------|-------|--------|\n| API endpoints | `services/api-service/tests/test_protocol_api.py` | ~15 tests | pytest |\n| Review workflow | `services/api-service/tests/test_review_api.py` | ~10 tests | pytest |\n| Auth | `services/api-service/tests/test_auth_required.py` | ~5 tests | pytest |\n| Exports | `services/api-service/tests/test_exports.py` | 36 tests | pytest |\n| Data integrity | `services/api-service/tests/test_integrity.py` | ~5 tests | pytest |\n| Quality scoring | `services/api-service/tests/test_quality.py` | ~5 tests | pytest |\n| Models/schemas | `services/api-service/tests/test_models.py`, `test_schemas.py` | ~10 tests | pytest |\n| UMLS clients | `services/api-service/tests/test_umls_clients.py` | ~5 tests | pytest |\n| Event contracts | `libs/events-py/tests/` | ~5 tests | pytest |\n| Pipeline nodes | None | 0 | — |\n| UI components | None | 0 | — |\n\n**Run all tests**: `make test`\n\n## Top 5 Risks for Maintainers\n\n### 1. Cross-Service Import Coupling\n\nPipeline nodes (`protocol-processor-service`) directly import from `api-service` for database access (`from api_service.storage import engine`). This creates a tight runtime coupling — the processor cannot run without the api-service package on the Python path.\n\n**Mitigation**: The `pyproject.toml` pythonpath config handles this for dev. For production, both packages must be installed together.\n\n### 2. No Pipeline Node Tests\n\nThe 7 LangGraph nodes have zero test coverage. All testing is through the API layer. A change to a node could break the pipeline without any test failure.\n\n**Mitigation**: Add integration tests that invoke individual nodes with mock LLM responses.\n\n### 3. Outbox Polling Latency\n\nThe outbox processor polls every 2 seconds. Under load, this could create a backlog. There's no back-pressure mechanism.\n\n**Mitigation**: Monitor outbox table depth; consider reducing poll interval or switching to PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY.\n\n### 4. Gemini API Rate Limits\n\nMultiple pipeline nodes call Gemini concurrently (semaphore=4 per node). A burst of protocol uploads could hit API rate limits.\n\n**Mitigation**: The circuit breaker (`pybreaker`) handles transient failures. Consider adding global rate limiting.\n\n### 5. Expression Tree vs Flat SQL Mismatch\n\nThe CIRCE and FHIR exporters walk the expression tree correctly, but the SQL exporter uses a flat model. Users may get inconsistent results across export formats.\n\n**Mitigation**: Document the limitation clearly (done). Future: implement tree-aware SQL generation using recursive CTE grouping.\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created status/index.md\"",
  "description": "Create docs/status/index.md"
}

{
  "command": "cat > /Users/noahdolevelixir/Code/medgemma-hackathon/docs/code-tour/index.md << 'DOCEOF'\n# Code Tour\n\nA linear walkthrough of the key code paths in ElixirTrials, from upload to review. Each \"slide\" covers one critical module.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 1: Upload Dialog\n\n> **As a researcher**, I want to upload a protocol PDF so the system can extract its eligibility criteria.\n\n**File**: `apps/hitl-ui/src/components/ProtocolUploadDialog.tsx`\n\n```tsx\nconst uploadMutation = useUploadProtocol();\n\nconst handleUpload = useCallback(async () => {\n    if (!selectedFile) return;\n    try {\n        await uploadMutation.mutateAsync({ file: selectedFile });\n        setSelectedFile(null);\n        onOpenChange(false);\n    } catch (err) {\n        setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Upload failed');\n    }\n}, [selectedFile, uploadMutation, onOpenChange]);\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: The upload dialog is the entry point for all protocol processing. It validates PDF type and 50 MB size limit client-side before hitting the API. The `useUploadProtocol` hook handles the two-step signed URL flow (upload → confirm).\n\n---\n\n## Slide 2: Protocol Upload API\n\n> **As the API**, I create a protocol record and generate a signed URL for direct browser-to-storage upload.\n\n**File**: `services/api-service/src/api_service/protocols.py:136`\n\n```python\n@router.post(\"/upload\", response_model=UploadResponse)\ndef upload_protocol(body: UploadRequest, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):\n    signed_url, gcs_path = generate_upload_url(\n        filename=body.filename, content_type=body.content_type,\n    )\n    protocol = Protocol(title=title, file_uri=gcs_path, status=\"uploaded\")\n    db.add(protocol)\n    db.commit()\n    return UploadResponse(protocol_id=protocol.id, upload_url=signed_url, ...)\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: The upload is a two-phase process. Phase 1 creates the DB record and returns a signed URL. Phase 2 (`confirm-upload`) triggers processing via the outbox. This prevents processing a file that was never actually uploaded.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 3: Outbox Wiring\n\n> **As the API service**, I connect the outbox processor to the pipeline trigger at startup.\n\n**File**: `services/api-service/src/api_service/main.py:81-93`\n\n```python\nprocessor = OutboxProcessor(\n    engine=engine,\n    handlers={\n        \"protocol_uploaded\": [handle_protocol_uploaded],\n    },\n)\ntask = asyncio.create_task(processor.start())\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: This is the bridge between the synchronous API world and the async pipeline. The outbox pattern ensures at-least-once delivery — if the API crashes after writing the outbox event but before the handler runs, the event will be picked up on restart. Note: `criteria_extracted` was removed in v2.0; `protocol_uploaded` is the only event.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 4: Pipeline Trigger\n\n> **As the outbox processor**, I dispatch events to the LangGraph pipeline.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/trigger.py:214`\n\n```python\ndef handle_protocol_uploaded(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n    thread_id = f\"{protocol_id}:{uuid4()}\"\n    initial_state = {\n        \"protocol_id\": payload[\"protocol_id\"],\n        \"file_uri\": payload[\"file_uri\"],\n        \"title\": payload[\"title\"],\n        \"status\": \"processing\",\n        \"error\": None,\n        \"errors\": [],\n        ...\n    }\n    config = {\"configurable\": {\"thread_id\": thread_id}}\n    asyncio.run(_run_pipeline(initial_state, config, payload))\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: The trigger bridges sync (outbox handler) to async (LangGraph) via `asyncio.run()`. Each run gets a unique `thread_id` (protocol_id + uuid4) to prevent checkpoint collision on re-extraction. The thread_id is stored in protocol metadata for retry support.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 5: Ingest Node\n\n> **As the first pipeline node**, I fetch the PDF bytes from storage.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/ingest.py`\n\n```python\nasync def ingest_node(state: PipelineState) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    pdf_bytes = await fetch_pdf_bytes(state[\"file_uri\"])\n    # Update protocol status in DB\n    with Session(engine) as session:\n        protocol = session.get(Protocol, state[\"protocol_id\"])\n        protocol.status = \"extracting\"\n        session.commit()\n    return {\"pdf_bytes\": pdf_bytes, \"status\": \"processing\"}\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: Ingest is the first node with external I/O (storage fetch). If the file doesn't exist or storage is down, this is where it fails — with a clear `error` that routes the pipeline to END.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 6: Extract Node\n\n> **As the extract node**, I send the PDF to Gemini and get structured criteria back.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/extract.py`\n\n```python\nasync def extract_node(state: PipelineState) -> dict[str, Any]:\n    result = await extract_criteria_structured(\n        pdf_bytes=state[\"pdf_bytes\"],\n        protocol_title=state[\"title\"],\n    )\n    return {\n        \"extraction_json\": json.dumps(result),\n        \"pdf_bytes\": None,  # Clear to reduce checkpoint size\n        \"status\": \"processing\",\n    }\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: This is the core AI step — Gemini 2.5 Flash reads the PDF and returns structured JSON with inclusion/exclusion criteria, categories, and confidence scores. The `pdf_bytes` are explicitly cleared after extraction to keep LangGraph checkpoints small.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 7: Parse Node\n\n> **As the parse node**, I create database records and decompose criteria into entities.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/parse.py`\n\n```python\n# Phase A: Create batch and criteria records\nbatch = CriteriaBatch(protocol_id=protocol_id)\nsession.add(batch)\nfor item in criteria_list:\n    criterion = Criteria(batch_id=batch.id, text=item[\"text\"], ...)\n    session.add(criterion)\n\n# Phase B: Async entity decomposition (outside DB session)\ntasks = [decompose_entities_from_criterion(c) for c in criteria]\nresults = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: Parse separates DB persistence (fast, transactional) from LLM decomposition (slow, parallelized). Entity decomposition runs with a semaphore of 4 to limit concurrent Gemini calls. The DB session is closed before LLM calls to avoid holding connections during I/O.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 8: Ground Node\n\n> **As the ground node**, I link entities to standard terminologies using dual grounding.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/ground.py`\n\n```python\nasync def _ground_entity_with_retry(entity, semaphore):\n    async with semaphore:\n        # Dual grounding: UMLS + OMOP in parallel\n        umls_result, omop_result = await asyncio.gather(\n            terminology_router.search(entity),\n            omop_mapper.resolve(entity),\n        )\n        result = _reconcile_dual_grounding(umls_result, omop_result)\n\n        # Agentic retry if confidence < 0.5\n        if result.confidence < 0.5:\n            for attempt in range(3):\n                # MedGemma reasoning loop\n                ...\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: Grounding is the most complex node — dual sourcing, reconciliation, and agentic retries. Error accumulation means one failed entity doesn't block the others. This is where the system gets the SNOMED, LOINC, RxNorm, and OMOP codes needed for export.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 9: Structure Node\n\n> **As the structure node**, I build expression trees from grounded criteria.\n\n**File**: `services/protocol-processor-service/src/protocol_processor/nodes/structure.py`\n\n```python\ntree = await build_expression_tree(\n    criterion_text=criterion.text,\n    field_mappings=field_mappings,\n    criterion_id=criterion.id,\n    protocol_id=protocol_id,\n    inclusion_exclusion=inclusion_exclusion,\n    session=session,\n)\ncriterion.structured_criterion = tree.model_dump()\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: Structure transforms flat criteria into queryable expression trees. Gemini detects AND/OR/NOT logic, then the builder creates `AtomicCriterion`, `CompositeCriterion`, and `CriterionRelationship` records. These trees power the CIRCE and FHIR exports.\n\n---\n\n## Slide 10: Review Page\n\n> **As a clinician**, I review extracted criteria side-by-side with the source PDF.\n\n**File**: `apps/hitl-ui/src/screens/ReviewPage.tsx`\n\n```tsx\n<PanelGroup direction=\"horizontal\">\n    <Panel defaultSize={50}>\n        <PdfViewer\n            url={pdfData.url}\n            targetPage={activeCriterion?.page_number ?? null}\n            highlightText={activeCriterion?.text ?? null}\n        />\n    </Panel>\n    <PanelResizeHandle />\n    <Panel defaultSize={50}>\n        {inclusionCriteria.map((c) => (\n            <CriterionCard\n                criterion={c}\n                onAction={handleAction}\n                onCriterionClick={handleCriterionClick}\n                isActive={activeCriterion?.id === c.id}\n            />\n        ))}\n    </Panel>\n</PanelGroup>\n```\n\n**Why this matters**: The review page is where human judgment meets AI output. Clicking a criterion scrolls the PDF to the source page and highlights the text. Criteria are grouped by inclusion/exclusion with pending items sorted first. The progress bar shows overall review completion.\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created code-tour/index.md\"",
  "description": "Create docs/code-tour/index.md"
}

Get an API key from [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)\n2. Add to `.env`:\n\n```bash\nGOOGLE_API_KEY=your-key-here\nGEMINI_MODEL_NAME=gemini-2.5-flash   # default\n```\n\n### Verify\n\n```bash\nmake verify-gemini\n```\n\nThis runs `scripts/verify_gemini_access.py` which makes a test call to the Gemini API.\n\n## Vertex AI (MedGemma)\n\nUsed for agentic grounding retry loop (MedGemma reasoning).\n\n### Setup\n\n1. Create a GCP project with Vertex AI enabled\n2. Deploy MedGemma to a Vertex AI endpoint\n3. Configure Application Default Credentials:\n\n```bash\ngcloud auth application-default login\nmake setup-adc    # Sets quota project from .env\n```\n\n4. Add to `.env`:\n\n```bash\nMODEL_BACKEND=vertex\nREDACTED\nGCP_REGION=europe-west4\nVERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID=your-endpoint-id\n```\n\n### ADC Setup Script\n\nThe `make setup-adc` command runs `scripts/setup-gcloud-adc.sh`, which:\n\n1. Reads `GCP_PROJECT_ID` or `GOOGLE_CLOUD_QUOTA_PROJECT` from `.env`\n2. Sets the quota project on your Application Default Credentials\n3. Required when using user-level ADC (not service accounts) for Vertex AI\n\n### Docker Compose\n\nFor Docker deployment, ADC credentials are mounted as a read-only volume:\n\n```yaml\nvolumes:\n  - ${GOOGLE_ADC_PATH:-~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json}:/tmp/keys/application_default_credentials.json:ro\nenvironment:\n  - REDACTED.json\n```\n\n## Google OAuth (UI Login)\n\nFor the HITL UI authentication:\n\n1. Create OAuth 2.0 credentials at [GCP Console → APIs & Services → Credentials](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials)\n2. Set redirect URI to `http://localhost:8000/auth/callback`\n3. Add to `.env`:\n\n```bash\nGOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id\nGOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=[REDACTED]\n```\n\nOAuth is optional for local development — the API works without it configured.\n\n## Environment Variable Reference\n\n| Variable | Required for | Default |\n|----------|-------------|---------|\n| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | Gemini Developer API | — |\n| `GEMINI_MODEL_NAME` | Gemini model selection | `gemini-2.5-flash` |\n| `MODEL_BACKEND` | Backend selection | (Gemini Developer API) |\n| `GCP_PROJECT_ID` | Vertex AI | — |\n| `GCP_REGION` | Vertex AI | `europe-west4` |\n| `VERTEX_ENDPOINT_ID` | MedGemma endpoint | — |\n| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | OAuth login | — |\n| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | OAuth login | — |\n| `GCLOUD_PROFILE` | gcloud config profile | — |\n| `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` | Experiment tracking | `http://localhost:5001` |\n| `UMLS_API_KEY` | UMLS grounding | — |\nDOCEOF\necho \"Created development/gemini-vertex-auth.md\"",

    10→from __future__ import annotations

    12→import re
